title: Adopt credit-based consumer flow with graceful redelivery for Redis/Kafka workers
creator: Priya Patel
description: Problem: Current consumer adapters rely on coarse interval-based redelivery and simple backoff timers that cause head-of-line blocking, tenant unfairness, and bursty retry storms. Several hotspots in the async pipeline (ingress, consumer-shim, retry orchestration) are tightly coupled and make it hard to reason about per-tenant concurrency limits. Goal: Introduce a credit-based delivery gate (a small, lightweight flow-control coordinator + consumer-side credit accounting) that decouples delivery pacing from retry timers, enforces per-tenant and per-route concurrency budgets, and supports graceful redelivery semantics across Redis Streams and Kafka consumers. Expected outcomes: lower P95/99 latency under congestion, reduced duplicate work from aggressive retries, and clearer observability for per-tenant throttling decisions. Scope: implement new consumer-shim changes, add a flow-control coordinator (co-located and optional global mode), integrate with Redis Streams XGROUP/XACK patterns and Kafka pause/resume APIs, add end-to-end metrics and feature flags for progressive rollout. Includes tests, benchmarks, and runbook updates.
comments: 2026-02-22 — Kickoff: sketched credit allocator API. Decided credits are small integer grants (default 4) issued per-tenant/route pair. Rationale: keeps allocator simple, avoids per-request RPCs when stable.

2026-02-25 — Design review with infra and platform: trade-offs discussed. Centralized allocator simplifies global fairness but is a single coord. Agreed to implement hybrid mode: local token bucket per-worker with periodic reconciliation to an allocator service (global optional).

2026-03-02 — Spike results: benchmarked local-only token bucket vs hybrid allocator under artificial tenant skew. Hybrid reduced tail latency by ~18% at 95th and reduced cross-tenant interference. Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1287

2026-03-04 — Implementation notes: consumer-shim will expose a small lifecycle API: request_credit(n), release_credit(n), report_processing_start(id), report_processing_done(id, success). For Kafka, we use pause/resume on the partition and only commit offsets once processing_done(true). For Redis Streams, adopt XACK after processing_done(true); keep visibility timeouts shorter because credits prevent hot loops.

2026-03-06 — Retry semantics: Instead of immediate requeue/backoff timers on error, failed items go to a per-route soft-queue with progressive backoff controlled by the allocator (max retry window configurable). Duplicate suppression: add a lightweight idempotency hint header to reduce repeated processing for semi-idempotent handlers.

2026-03-08 — Observability: added metrics plan — credit_grants_total, credit_used, credit_releases, per-tenant queue_depth_estimate, retry_rate, redelivery_latency. Dashboards: link to draft: https://app.datadog.com/dash/async/credit-flow-overview (internal).

2026-03-10 — PR opened for consumer-shim and Kafka pause/resume integration: https://github.com/redwood-inference/worker/pull/4321. Unit tests added for credit accounting and integration tests using localstack for Redis streams and testcontainers for Kafka.

2026-03-12 — QA notes from Diego Alvarez: found an edge where a worker crash could leak credits if not reconciled; mitigation: allocator now supports periodic lease reclamation (grants TTL) and reconciler job reclaims stale grants. Added follow-up ticket for making grants lease shorter in noisy clusters.

2026-03-13 — Rollout plan approved by SRE and Product: feature flag 'credit_flow_v1' gated by route. Canary to 5% of traffic in staging, monitor P95, retry_rate, and dups. If regressions >10% on P95 or retry_rate increases, roll back. Post-canary, 25% for 48h, then gradual ramp.

Follow-ups: 1) Evaluate integrating allocator with Dedicated autoscaler signals (ENG-XXXXX). 2) Create a migration guide for customers running private deployments; consider a lightweight coordinator mode that runs as a sidecar. 3) Audit downstream handlers for idempotency; create a doc for best practices.
Risks: small added complexity in consumer-shim and a new component (allocator). Mitigations: hybrid mode, TTL on grants, exhaustive e2e tests, and a conservative default credit size.
